findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed there to be no signed employee health reporting agreements available for verification during the inspection. CORRECTED - Inspector provided employee reporting agreement form to the PIC to have all employees sign. Ensure that all current and future employees sign an employee health reporting agreement that is stored at the facility to be checked during future inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed knife sanitizing dip well to have no level of detectable chlorine in solution. Discussed possible causes with PIC. PIC stated that the sanitizer was prepared at 8:00am. Discussed evaporation of CL and also sanitizer reduction with use of sanitizer. PIC changed out the sanitizer immediately for solution measuring 100 PPM CL. Ensure solution is tested regularly to prevent food contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of food debris around the corners of the walk-in cooler. Discussed possible cleaning measures with PIC; cleaning will likely require shelves to be removed from the cooler. Ensure this area is added to a regular cleaning schedule to prevent the build up of food soils and debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
No CFM was present on site at time of follow-up.  A CFM shall be present during hours of operation.

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Employees at time of inspection were not Certified Food Managers, or have current Food Handlers certificates.  Because of the large amount of priority and priority foundation violations, this facility is out of compliance for this violation. 
*Post inspection note*
The priority and priority foundation line violations were corrected at the end of the inspection and removed. However, the PIC was unaware of where the necessary documents were located. Paperwork and documentation should be readily available during routine inspections.

2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Black coving is missing from the wall and floor juncture directly across from the mop sink.  Junctures shall be coved to prevent soil and food accumulation.  Ensure coving is replaced to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Areas in need of a sealant or caulk include:
-(REPEAT) Along the top and around the mop sink
-(REPEAT) Along the top and around the 3 part sink
 These areas shall be easily cleanable, non absorbent, and smooth to prevent soil accumulation and pest entry.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The caulk along the top of the 3 part sink is cracking and wearing away directly above the sink basins.  The caulk missing in this area allows water and debris to get trapped under the present caulk and behind the sink.  Ensure the sink is re-caulked to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Employees present at time of inspection do not have Food Handlers Certifications.  All employees handling food must obtain either a Food Handlers Certification or a Certified Food Protection Manager Certificate within 30 days of hire.  Ensure all new and present employees are current on their certifications.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Proper use of restriction and exclusion
findings.comment:
No paperwork regarding employee reporting, exclusion, or restriction were found at time of inspection.  Keep this paperwork and information on-site and available for future inspections.  Inspector will follow-up on 1/16/2023.

2-201.13: The PERSON IN CHARGE shall adhere to the following conditions when removing, adjusting, or retaining the EXCLUSION or RESTRICTION of a FOOD EMPLOYEE (see Code for detail).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
Information regarding proper clean up procedures to vomiting or diarrheal occurrences were not found at time of inspection.  Keep this paperwork and information on-site and available for future inspections and guidance for employees.  Inspector will address this violation at the 1/16/2023 follow-up.  If the facility does not have a copy, one will be provided at that time.

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Mouse feces were observed at time of inspection.  Droppings were found in the cabinet under the Icee machine and also in the cabinet under the tea and soda machine in the dining area.  Ensure pest control company is contacted to eradicate rodents in a timely manner to prevent contamination.

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

Employee illness policy is not able to be presented in a verifiable manner via a written policy. Discussed employee illness information with PIC Kelly. Ensure documentation is maintained at establishment via a training or personnel binder for inspectors to review upon inspection. Ensure employees are trained periodically on reporting responsibilities for foodborne illness. Provided PIC documentation of foodborne illness policy and reporting agreements. Norovirus cleanup policy was provided as well.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Two containers of tuna, 1 container of green bell peppers, and 1 container of cucumber bear a "use-by" date mark of 5/19. These foods are expired and must be discarded. PIC voluntarily discarded foods at time of inspection. 
Subway policy has a maximum date mark of 5 days for prepped food items.

Mop observed stored within bucket in mop sink area. Ensure mops are hung to air dry to prevent possible bacteria growth.
